synopsis: The corpus associates Zhao with on-road research on accelerated simulation and statistical assessment of autonomous-vehicle testing [f1295, f6847, f6900]. In 2016, University of Michigan researchers Zhao, Peng and colleagues used importance sampling to make rare crash and conflict events more frequent in simulation, then statistically reweighted the results [f1295]. A 2017 IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems publication by Zhao, Huang, Peng and colleagues reported very large acceleration for lane-change conflict estimation, although no numerical acceleration factor is supplied here [f6847]. Separately, an ISSRE 2019 conservative Bayesian analysis by Zhao, Robu, Flynn, Salako and Strigini found road-testing assessments highly sensitive to the prior; the supplied facts do not establish whether this finding directly qualifies the accelerated-evaluation results [f6900, f6847].

relations.note: Adds a published lane-change application and acceleration finding to the accelerated-simulation research.
